# Run log: fornax_pilot_20261113

## Stage 0 preflight: PASS (6/6 gates)

- Snapshot: 22 bubbletea files, hashes in reference/manifest.json.
- Selector: JSON re-implementation equals bubbletea's stored scores on 45,402 M60 sources (max difference 0.0, no
  decision mismatch). scikit-learn is not needed.
- Services: Gaia (Data Lab) 5 s, Euclid TAP 6 s, Euclid cutout 10 s, Legacy DR11 LSDB 69 s for a 1' cone (slow to
  open), Legacy cutout layers ls-dr11-south and ls-dr10 both return real images.
- Control field: RA 53.303, Dec -40.944 (5.59 deg from NGC 1399, b = -54.1 vs -53.6, coverage 1.00, Gaia count
  11,322 vs 11,358). 36 of 755 grid points were eligible.
- Problem: the ESA Gaia archive answered HTTP 429 (rate limit, no Retry-After) after ~10 anonymous queries; pyvo then
  waited silently and the stage hung for 10 min. Fix: Gaia now comes from the NOIRLab Data Lab copy (bubbletea's
  production route; Q3C cones, declination strips, exact count checks). ESA is kept as a documented fallback.
- Lesson: Data Lab returns source_id through a masked column that pandas turns into float; the id is now taken from
  the astropy table as int64.
- Consequence: stage order changes to 0, 2, 3, 1, 4, ... because the empirical part of the limits study (stellar
  locus, Gaia completeness) needs the Gaia and Euclid tables of the control field.
- Observation from the field map: DR1 has a coverage gap just east of the Fornax field (RA 56-57.5); most of the 44
  Saifollahi candidates lie outside the 1 deg field.

## Stage 2 Gaia retrieval and scoring: PASS (4/4 gates)

- Rows: fornax 11,358, control 11,322 (equal to the count queries; no duplicate ids). Retrieval 4.5 min (Data Lab).
- Selector passed: control 1,555 (495 per deg2; bubbletea 95% range for this latitude band is 191-522, so the control
  field is on the high side but inside). Most selected sources are faint (G > 20) and lack 5-parameter astrometry.
- Known Fornax objects in the 1 deg field (consistency check only): 165 confirmed, of which 64 have a Gaia source
  within 0.5" (G = 19.3-21.7, median 20.6; none brighter than G = 19) and 56 of those 64 pass the selector.
  The 8 misses: 3 two-parameter sources at G > 21 with probability 0.37-0.72, 3 just below threshold (0.60-0.83),
  1 with a formally significant proper motion (11.7 sigma at G = 20.3) and 1 with zero excess noise (r_h 5.6 pc).
- Voggel-style cuts select nothing among the known objects because they require G < 19; at 20 Mpc that route is
  empty. Recorded as a comparison column only.
- Lesson: at Fornax distance the whole known population sits in Gaia's last 2 magnitudes, where the selected cloud
  is also densest in the control field. Euclid has to do the separation there.
- Consequence for Stage 3: the object with an 11.7 sigma Gaia proper motion is a direct test case for the
  Gaia-to-Euclid displacement.

## Stage 3 Euclid cross-match and displacement: PASS on retry 1 (first attempt failed 1 fatal gate)

First attempt (failed): 1.0" match radius gave 1.3-1.6% displaced-position (chance) matches (limit 1%); only 64% of
Fornax Gaia sources had a Euclid entry; the 3-sigma displacement flag had 20% false flags on non-moving sources.

Diagnosis and fixes (no criterion loosened):
- Match radius: 99% of true matches lie within 0.47". The radius is now calibrated automatically: the largest of
  1.0, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3" with a chance-match rate below 1% in both fields. Adopted 0.7" (0.60% / 0.71%).
- Coverage: the eastern third of the Fornax field has a DR1 mosaic tile (102035564, VIS + NIR) but ZERO catalogue
  entries. The tile-polygon footprint MOC (94% covered) therefore overestimates the usable area. Coverage is now
  defined per Gaia source from the catalogue itself (any MER entry within 20"): fornax 65.3%, control 98.2%.
  Inside coverage 95.9% / 97.5% of Gaia sources with 17 < G < 20.5 have an entry.
- Download: joining the morphology and PHZ tables inside a cone query took > 6 min for a 5' cone; now the catalogue is
  fetched by cone (8 declination strips, ~4.5 min per field, 305k rows with I_E < 24) and the other tables by
  object_id lists (1000 ids per query, ~6 s each).

Displacement test (user comment 2: an opportunity):
- Per-tile fit of baseline and frame offset from stars: baseline 8.99-9.12 yr (median 9.06, i.e. Euclid epoch about
  2025.06, not 2024.6 as guessed in the plan), frame offsets up to 6.6 mas, 38 tiles.
- Scatter per axis after removing Gaia proper motion: 5.9 mas for G < 19.5, 7.0 at G ~ 19.9, 10.7 at G ~ 20.6. The
  5.7-6 mas floor is Euclid mosaic astrometry (0.06 pixel), independent of magnitude. This corresponds to a
  proper-motion sensitivity of about 0.65-0.85 mas/yr per axis.
- Threshold scan (stars and compact non-moving sources only): at 4 sigma, 99.0% of stars expected to move by more
  than 5 sigma are recovered and 3.6% of compact non-moving sources are falsely flagged. Adopted 4 sigma; VALIDATED
  for compact sources. For extended sources ~50% are flagged because the Gaia and Euclid centroids differ, so the
  flag must not be read as motion for galaxies.
- Selector-passed sources WITHOUT any Gaia proper motion: most of the compact ones show a significant displacement,
  i.e. they are faint moving stars that the Gaia-only selector cannot remove. This is the gain from comment 2.
- Known confirmed objects (consistency only): 47 have a Euclid entry inside coverage; a few show a displacement
  (one very large). They are listed for review in the run log of stage 5, not removed here.

What the compactness figure shows: stars form a tight locus at mu_max - mag ~ -3; galaxies form a separate sequence;
the known Fornax objects lie in between (-2.7 to -1.2, Sersic radius 0.05-0.4"), a region that is almost empty in
the control field. Gaia G is 0.5-1.4 mag fainter than Euclid Kron I_E for these objects (G misses extended flux).

Lessons: (1) never use tile polygons as coverage; (2) calibrate radius and thresholds from controls inside the
stage; (3) avoid multi-table cone joins on the Euclid TAP.

## Stage 4 Legacy Surveys DR11 South: PASS on retry 1 (first attempt failed 1 fatal gate)

- First attempt: nearest Tractor entry within 1" gave a 4.1% chance-match rate (the catalogue has 510k entries per
  field). Fix: Tractor is built on Gaia DR3 (ref_cat = G3, ref_id = source_id), so the match is by that id
  (fornax 11,297 of 11,358; control 11,286 of 11,322; no chance matches possible) and only the remaining 59 / 35
  sources use a positional match among entries brighter than 23.5, radius calibrated to 0.7" (0.9% chance rate).
- Download through LSDB: 82 s and 70 s per 1 deg field, 51 columns. Median epoch 2016.4 (same as Gaia).
- Depth (5 sigma, point source): g 25.4, r 25.1, z 23.8.
- Legacy has no hole: all Gaia sources of the Fornax field have grz, while only 65% have Euclid entries.
- Legacy total minus MER DECam 2-FWHM aperture for stars: -0.27, -0.26, -0.26, -0.25 mag in g, r, i, z with
  0.016 mag scatter: a constant aperture loss, so colours from the two sources agree.
- DR11 versus DR10 (bubbletea) for 181 known Fornax objects: offsets 0.008, -0.001, -0.001 mag in g, r, z; same
  Tractor type for 91%.
- Tractor types of selector-passed sources: SER dominates (galaxies); caveat: Tractor forces PSF for Gaia sources
  with low excess noise, so type is not independent of Gaia.
- Colour-colour: known Fornax objects form a tight clump (g-r ~ 0.55-0.8, r-z ~ 0.3-0.6) at the edge of the stellar
  locus and away from the red galaxy spur. The colour box for stage 5 is nevertheless taken from Virgo objects.

## Stage 1 limits: PASS (run after stages 2-4; second run after cleaning the star sample)

- Gaia 50% completeness in Euclid I_E (control field, clean isolated Euclid sources): 20.8 for point-like, 20.7 for
  marginally resolved, 19.7 for resolved sources. Gaia loses resolved sources about 1 mag earlier.
- Stellar locus in mu_max - mag: median -2.97, scatter 0.12 mag, 99% quantile only 0.25-0.32 mag above the median
  for 17.5 < I_E < 21 (10 bins, 80-820 clean single stars each). First version used det_quality_flag = 0 only and
  lost all stars brighter than I_E = 18.5 (they sit inside their own star mask); now the star-mask and blend bits are
  allowed and RUWE, multi-peak and non-single-star cuts define "clean single stars".
- Empirical VIS PSF from 24 stacked stars: simulated point source mu_max - mag = -2.85 versus observed -2.97
  (stack slightly broadened by the shifts); only the differential shift is used.
- Simulated shift for King (c = 30) profiles: 0.36 mag at r_h = 0.05", 0.73 at 0.10", 1.32 at 0.20", 3.6 at 1.0".
  Smallest r_h separated from 99% of stars: 0.04" (4 pc at 20 Mpc, 10 pc at 50 Mpc) for 17.5 < I_E < 21.
- At 20 Mpc: M_V = -12, -11 are within Gaia's reach (I_E 19.1, 20.1); M_V = -10 (I_E 21.1) is not. A Gaia-seeded
  search at Fornax distance therefore stops near M_V ~ -10.5; at 50 Mpc near -12.5. Euclid resolution is NOT the
  limiting factor for classical UCDs (r_h >= 10 pc) out to 50 Mpc; Gaia detection is.
- Gaia G is fainter than Euclid Kron I_E by 0.5-1.4 mag for resolved compact sources, so a G-based luminosity
  underestimates them.
- Sersic radius and PSF-minus-Kron quantiles of stars are noisy (failed fits); compactness is the primary size
  indicator, Sersic radius is supporting information.
- Not done: Gaia excess noise versus angular size for Virgo objects worked only as a positional join; see the
  summary for the number of objects. Gaia's upper size limit for detection is not quantified.

## Stage 5 cut flow and tiers: PASS (3/3 gates)

Cut flow (sources; Euclid-dependent steps use the covered area: fornax 2.05 deg2, control 3.09 deg2):

| step | cut | control | fornax | known confirmed surviving |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | all Gaia | 11322 | 11358 | 64 |
| 1 | frozen selector | 1501 | 1414 | 56 |
| 2 | no Gaia motion above 5 sigma | 1430 | 1330 | 56 |
| 3 | Euclid entry inside coverage | 1344 | 783 | 40 |
| 4 | Euclid quality | 1294 | 753 | 40 |
| 5 | not a compact displaced star | 1253 | 722 | 40 |
| 6 | resolved (above 99% of stars) | 1230 | 698 | 40 |
| 7 | size up to 100 pc at 20 Mpc | 492 | 337 | 39 |
| 8 | round | 377 | 285 | 39 |
| 9 | Legacy colour box (Virgo reference) | 43 | 117 | 38 |

- Control density: 478 per deg2 after the Gaia selector, 13.9 after all cuts (factor 34), 5.5 for tier A.
- Tiers (fornax / control): A 95 / 17, B 22 / 26, C 175 / 341, D 57 / 4. A = all cuts and size up to the 95th
  percentile of reference UCDs outside Fornax (52.6 pc = 0.54" at 20 Mpc, n = 372); B = larger, up to 100 pc;
  C = exactly one of roundness or colour failed; D = outside Euclid coverage (Gaia + Legacy only).
- First version had a single tier A (117 / 43); the control objects sat at 0.3-1.0", so the size class was split
  using the reference population (not Fornax). No known object moved out of tier A.
- Verification: of 64 known confirmed objects with a Gaia source, 8 fail the frozen Gaia selector, 16 are outside
  Euclid catalogue coverage (4 of them reach tier D), 1 fails the size cut, 1 the colour box, 38 are tier A.
  So 38 of 40 (95%) that reach the Euclid cuts are recovered, and 38 of 64 (59%) overall.
- Tier A in Fornax: 38 known confirmed, 25 from the 'rejected' class of bubbletea (spectroscopic Fornax compact
  objects that are not UCDs by definition, mostly globular clusters), 6 'uncertain', 26 not in the catalogue.
- Galaxy sequence (information only): background galaxies follow a tight compactness-magnitude sequence. Its 5%
  lower envelope was measured on the northern control half. Tier A below that envelope: fornax 74 (32 of the 38
  known), control evaluation half 2 in 1.54 deg2. Defined only for I_E < 20 (flat extrapolation beyond).
- Photo-z and PHZ classes (information, never used): tier A objects are PHZ class 'galaxy' with photo-z ~ 0.2 and
  globular-cluster probability 0 in both fields, i.e. useless for this purpose, as the user expected.
- Not applied: Euclid colour cut (no reference sample outside Fornax with Euclid photometry).


## Stage 6 spatial statistics: PASS (2/2 gates)

- Effective area, three independent estimates agree: fornax 65.4% (random points), 65.3% (30" grid cells), 65.3%
  (Gaia sources) of 3.14 deg2 = 2.05 deg2; control 98.1 / 97.8 / 98.2% = 3.08 deg2. The MER catalogue is also empty
  within about 1.5' of the centre of NGC 1399 (coverage 68% in the 0-3' annulus).
- Background (control field): tier A 17 objects = 5.5 per deg2 (68% interval 4.3-7.0); tier A below the galaxy
  sequence 2 objects in the evaluation half = 1.3 per deg2; tier A or B 14.0 per deg2. The control tier A objects
  are unevenly spread over eight sectors (0,1,1,1,5,3,5,1; dispersion index 1.7), so a 58% field-to-field term is
  used for tier A instead of bubbletea's 18%.
- Fornax, whole covered field: tier A 95 observed, 11.4 expected (3.3 sigma with the 58% term); tier A below the
  galaxy sequence 74 observed, 2.8 expected (> 8 sigma, numerical floor); tier A or B 117 observed, 28.7 expected
  (5.0 sigma).
- Radial profile: the excess is concentrated. Within 16' (93 kpc): 61 tier A against 1.2 expected. Densities fall
  from ~800 per deg2 at 3-6' to ~40 at 16-30' and reach the control level beyond ~30' (175 kpc). In the 0-3' bin
  only 2 tier A objects are found although 8 known confirmed objects with Gaia sources lie there: the galaxy core
  is not usable with the catalogue.
- Caveat: tier A is dominated by already known Fornax objects (38 confirmed UCDs, 25 other spectroscopic compact
  objects), so the excess mainly validates the method. 26 tier A objects are not in bubbletea's catalogue.
- Significances are not corrected for the choice of annuli.

## Stage 7 cutouts and visual triage: PASS (2/2 gates)

- 182 objects in 27 tiles: all have four Euclid bands (12" cutouts on the 0.1" grid) and a Legacy DR11 grz image.
  About 760 cutouts in 20 min with four parallel requests; the tile lookup (one archive query per tile) took 5 min.
  The `ls-dr11-south` viewer layer returned normal images (bubbletea had seen dark DR11 layers earlier).
- Eleven contact sheets: known confirmed (2), tier A not in the catalogue (2), tier A other known objects (2),
  tier B, control tier A, control tier B (2), control tier C sample.
- Visual notes by Claude (information only; tiers and ranks unchanged). Flags: clean_compact, uncertain,
  galaxy_like, blend, near_bright_star, nucleated_dwarf.
  - Known confirmed UCDs (first 24 inspected): 21 look alike: round, compact, soft halo in VIS, white to blue-white
    in grz. One is a nucleus inside a diffuse dwarf (the MER entry is the whole galaxy), one is a galaxy with an
    off-centre nucleus (fails the size cut), one is blended with red neighbours.
  - Fornax tier A not in the catalogue (26): 14 clean compact, 3 uncertain, 4 galaxy-like, 3 blends, 2 next to a
    bright star.
  - Fornax tier B (22): all galaxy-like (discs, spirals or rings, smooth dwarfs or background ellipticals). The
    large-size class adds no UCD-like object here.
  - Control tier A (17): 12 galaxy-like, 2 blends, 3 clean compact. So about 1 clean compact object per deg2
    survives everything in a field without a host.
- Not inspected: second known sheet, other known tier A objects, control tier B and C sheets.
- Lesson: the Euclid colour composite needs VIS smoothed to the NISP resolution, otherwise every compact core
  turns blue.

## Stage 8 synthesis: PASS (5/5 gates)

- Every stage has a passing verdict (stages 3 and 4 on their first retry). Disk use 0.5 GB of the 10 GB budget;
  sky area 6.3 deg2 of the 10 deg2 limit.
- Gaia pre-selection for future runs (`ucd/config/candidate_preselection.adql`): G range, excess-noise significance
  above 4, no parallax or proper motion above 5 sigma. In the two pilot fields it keeps 3,075 of 22,680 Gaia sources
  (factor 7.4 fewer), 159 of 160 tier A or B candidates and all 56 known confirmed objects that pass the selector.
  It must be validated on an independent field.
- Local report: runs/fornax_pilot_20261113/report/index.html. Final candidate tables with the visual notes:
  stage_8_report/tables/final_candidates_<field>.csv.

## Overall assessment of the first run

What works:
- Gaia (frozen selector) + Euclid compactness + Legacy colour reduce the control-field density from 478 to 5.5 per
  deg2 (tier A) and recover 38 of the 40 known Fornax UCDs that have Gaia and Euclid data.
- The Gaia-to-Euclid displacement is a usable proper-motion test (0.65-0.85 mas/yr per axis) and removes faint
  moving stars that have no Gaia proper motion.
- The cluster signal is recovered blind to the known objects: 61 tier A objects within 16' of NGC 1399 against 1.2
  expected.

What limits the method:
- Gaia detection, not Euclid resolution: at 20 Mpc the search stops near M_V ~ -10.5; only 64 of 165 known
  confirmed objects in the field have a Gaia source.
- Euclid catalogue coverage: 35% of the Fornax field and the core of NGC 1399 have no catalogue entries.
- The residual contaminants are compact galaxies on the bright, large side of the allowed size range.

Open questions for calibration (next sessions):
1. Make the galaxy-sequence envelope a cut? It keeps 32 of 38 known objects and leaves 2 control objects in 1.5 deg2.
2. Measure sizes directly on VIS cutouts at the Gaia position (PSF-convolved King fit) instead of using MER
   compactness, especially where MER shreds or merges (nucleated dwarfs, the galaxy core, the catalogue hole).
3. A Euclid colour criterion (I_E - Y, Y - H) needs a reference sample outside the target; tonight's known Fornax
   objects could define it for other fields.
4. Field-to-field variation of the background needs more than one control field.
5. Validate the pre-selection query and run a disc-galaxy field (NGC 1291 or NGC 1433) and Fornax A / Dorado.
